excerpt: Check Dubai's First-Time Home Buyer Programme eligibility, application steps, participating offers and costs using Dubai Land Department guidance.
introduction:
Dubai's First-Time Home Buyer Programme gives eligible UAE residents a route to benefits offered by participating developers and banks. Apply through Dubai Land Department (DLD) or Dubai REST, wait for eligibility confirmation and compare the actual offer and total cost before choosing a home.

DLD's published criteria and benefits can change. This guide reflects the official programme page checked on 8 November 2026; confirm current conditions and participating partners directly before applying or making a payment.
takeaways: DLD lists UAE residency, age 18 or older, no current Dubai freehold residential property and a property value below AED 5 million among its eligibility criteria.
Eligible applicants receive a DLD confirmation and QR code to use with participating providers.
There is no additional programme application fee, but standard registration and other transaction charges can still apply.

sections.heading: Who can apply?
sections.body:
DLD's [First-Time Home Buyer overview](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/first-time-home-buyer-overview/) states that applicants must be UAE residents of any nationality, at least 18, not currently own a freehold residential property in Dubai, and seek a property valued below AED 5 million. The limit is below AED 5 million, so do not assume a property at exactly that figure qualifies.

The official FAQ explains that owning a property in another emirate does not by itself prevent participation if the Dubai criterion is met. It also states that a person who purchased through the programme cannot use it again merely by selling that property. Check joint purchase and any other special circumstances with DLD.

Eligibility is assessed by the authority. A developer's advertisement or a preliminary discussion is not a confirmation that you qualify.

sections.heading: How do you apply?
sections.body:
DLD says to register through its website or the Dubai REST app and submit the requested information. If eligible, the applicant receives a confirmation email containing a programme QR code. Use that code when discussing participating offers with developers or banks. If DLD finds the application ineligible, it says applicants may reapply when circumstances change and they meet the criteria.

Prepare the information requested by the official application and use DLD's published channels. Check the origin of any third-party message and share identity or payment information only through official channels.

The chart shows the order of the application steps. The numbers are sequence markers, not waiting times, success rates or programme statistics.

sections.heading: What benefits may be available?
sections.body:
DLD lists early access to selected launches or inventory, preferential pricing from participating developers, financing offers and flexible payment of registration fees through eligible credit cards. The programme may also provide additional benefits for Emirati citizens. Individual offers depend on the participating organisation, property and the applicant's circumstances.

Ask for the actual written price, payment schedule, financing rate and all conditions. Compare them with alternative properties and ordinary bank offers on the same basis. Early access or a preferential label does not establish that a home is the best value for your needs.

DLD's [programme launch announcement](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/news-media/dubai-launches-landmark-initiative-further-enabling-first-time-homeownership) provides the initiative's background. Use the current overview and partner information for today's rules rather than relying only on the launch announcement.

sections.heading: What costs still need to be budgeted?
sections.body:
The programme page says there is no additional fee to apply or participate. It also says standard DLD registration fees and developer or bank charges continue to apply unless a specific offer states otherwise. A payment plan for a fee changes when it is paid; it does not necessarily remove the fee.

Request an itemised current quote for the exact property, including registration, any brokerage, lender charges, insurance, service charges and initial furnishing or repairs. Confirm the conditions of any eligible credit-card instalment plan with the provider.

If using a mortgage, ask the bank about eligibility, valuation, the amount financed, rates, repayments and early-settlement costs. Programme participation does not by itself guarantee a loan or approval for a particular property.

sections.heading: Compare the property, not just the programme offer
sections.body:
A ready home and an off-plan apartment have different inspection options and payment timing. For a ready unit, inspect its condition and review title, any lease, mortgage and building charges. For an off-plan unit, verify the registered project, developer, payment recipient, contracted specification and handover terms.

Consider the location and daily routine alongside the full cost. The [JVC and Arjan area comparison](/journal/jvc-vs-arjan-apartment-investment-comparison) offers a method for examining building-level differences; an investment example should not be treated as the cost of a home for your own use.

Keep a contingency for changes in circumstances. Do not commit to an instalment schedule that depends on an uncertain future event without understanding the consequences.

sections.heading: What happens after eligibility is confirmed?
sections.body:
Use the QR code with participating organisations and ask each provider to explain which properties and terms are covered. DLD's FAQ says the code remains valid until the buyer purchases and registers a property with DLD. It also describes restrictions for joint purchases and the use of participating partners, so check the current wording if you are applying with another person.

Keep the confirmation and written offer with your records. If your circumstances or selected property change, ask DLD to confirm whether the eligibility and offer still apply before relying on them. A QR code is not a title deed or proof that a property has been reserved.

sections.heading: Ask about current options
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Dubai project collection](/projects?emirate=Dubai) and ask which properties and programme offers are currently available. Ask for the programme terms and eligibility of the specific apartment you are considering.

[Contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget, preferred location and intended move date. Apply through DLD's official channel and confirm eligibility, partner terms and all costs before making a commitment.
